changes.old: The edict is not an inscription found inside present Kerala and states no regnal year. Dhammika dates the Girnar text to 257 BCE; Hultzsch's chronology (coronation about 264 BCE) gives about 252 BCE for the twelfth regnal year. Neither year is adopted. Its claims do not independently prove local medical installations.
changes.new: The edict is not an inscription found inside present Kerala and states no regnal year. Dhammika dates the Girnar text to 257 BCE; this is an attributed editorial date, not an adopted exact year. Hultzsch pp. xxxv–xxxvi does not establish a 252 BCE date for Edict II. Its claims do not independently prove local medical installations.

changes.old: The research institution supports the second-century date of the Geography; local passages and geographical identifications remain unverified. Geography 7.1.8 (Mouziris, an emporium) and 7.1.86 (Karoura, royal seat of Kerobothros) were read in McCrindle's 1885 translation. McCrindle, following Yule, identified Mouziris with Kodungallur and Karoura with Karur in Tamil Nadu; these are attributed identifications, and Ptolemy's coordinates are not modern positions.
changes.new: The research institution supports the second-century date of the Geography. Geography 7.1.8 (Mouziris, an emporium) and 7.1.86 (Karoura, royal seat of Kerobothros) were inspected in OCR of McCrindle’s 1885 English translation and commentary. McCrindle, following Yule, identified Mouziris with Kodungallur and Karoura with Karur in Tamil Nadu. These remain attributed identifications; original Greek, scan images and a modern critical edition were not verified. Ptolemy’s coordinates are not modern positions.
